messages:
maya: bump — ACME reported a regression after the last canary. Customer says the model starts dropping earlier instructions when the conversation context grows past ~8k tokens. They gave concrete examples where the system prompt and earlier user messages disappear from the reply. Escalating to eng-runtime. request_id: req-0a1b2c

tonny: looking. cc @alex @olivia. can you paste the exact payload + request id + model name?

maya: pasting payload and request_id (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-2-beta","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a highly concise summarizer. Always include the action items first."},{"role":"user","content":"<very long conversation ~10k tokens>"}]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
```
request_id: req-0a1b2c
customer note: they said redwood-1.9 did not exhibit this behavior; regression observed only after 2-beta canary.

deploybot: [deploy] canary rollout redwood-2-beta -> 2026-03-10T18:40Z (10% traffic)

tony: I just reproduced locally with a sanitized replay. logs show repeated KV eviction and context_offset jumps. snippet:
```text
[2026-03-10T18:41:12Z] model_session=ms-73 evict_kv_cache token_idx=8192 seq_len=16384
[2026-03-10T18:41:12Z] model_session=ms-73 context_offset jumped -12288 -> 4096
```
This looks like a sequence packing / offset bug where prefix KV entries are being overwritten when sequences cross an internal chunk boundary.

alex: that aligns with the recent batching optimization that packs variable-length requests into shared buffers. If offset math is wrong when a request spans the 8k chunk boundary, the runtime can write over earlier KV segments and effectively \"forget\" instructions. Immediate mitigation: rollback canary or pin impacted customers to redwood-1.9.

olivia: agreed. ops/SRE — can we revert the canary and pin the ACME account? I'll add a routing rule.

tony: created internal ticket RED-1256. rollback runbook (short):
1) scale canary -> 0%: `./scripts/rollout revert --deployment redwood-2-beta --percent 0`
2) pin customer: Console -> Routing -> add rule for acme.com -> model redwood-1.9
3) collect runtime debug bundle and attach to RED-1256 (`/opt/redwood/logs/runtime/*.log.gz`)

olivia: as a temporary workaround for larger customers we can also enforce `max_context_tokens=8192` on their account via the control plane to avoid triggering the packing scenario while we revert.

maya: I applied a temporary pin for ACME and told them we're investigating. any ETA on full revert?

tony: rollback started; ETA ~12 minutes. will upload debug artifacts to RED-1256 when complete. :eyes:

deploybot: [deployment] rollback start for redwood-2-beta at 2026-03-10T18:53Z by tony

alex: engineering follow-up: root cause confirmed — off-by-chunk bug in the batch packing layer miscomputes prefix offsets when a request crosses the internal 8k chunk boundary, causing silent KV layer overwrites. fix is in PR #5432; unit + integration tests added for chunk-boundary cases.

olivia: plan: full revert now, QA patch to staging with tests, then hotfix canary after verification. owners: tony (runtime), alex (batching), olivia (canary ops).

maya: thanks everyone. I informed the customer about the rollback and gave an ETA. I'll update them again once RED-1256 has the debug bundle and the revert completes. :thumbsup:
